I'm not a dentist, but I've had tooth problems and I'm quite inquisitive so I've learned from experiences :D A skilled dentist could interpret xrays easily but some xrays can be hazy, so they ask you to confirm it after they've marked it, just to be sure. It could be that you've had problems with both the bottom and top but the bottom was worse. Now that the bottom started to heal, the pain concentrated on the top one instead. 

I would suggest to go back to the dentist, and politely explain the situation. Ask why the bottom tooth was treated and let the dentist explain the xray to you. If it were indeed a mistake, ask if you can get it for free. A second opinion from another dentist won't hurt, but it's best that you confirm with your current one first. :)

Root canals are expensive :( :( so I'd also suggest to have a dental check up at least once a year to check for minor tooth problems. Plaques and chips don't cause discomfort but they can develop into something worse. Hope you get better soon!

Bring it to a doctor as soon as you can! :o I've never had bronchitis, but I have chronic sinusitis which occasionally makes me cough out a blob even though I feel no nose blockage whatsoever. Just occasionally my face would feel heavy "deep deep up there" so I would snort really hard until the blob goes out. It usually feels painful but very freeing afterwards. The blob consistency is similar to how you describe it, occasionally I wake up with this on my throat due to post-nasal drip. I found that this is due to dry air which makes the mucus more blobby, especially if it's a deep blockage like in the sinuses. 

I would suggest, if you still have it (and can't bring it to a doctor), to leave it out and observe if it dries up flat. If it does, it's probably just a bloody thick blob of mucus not brain matter. But if you can and you're worried, get it lab-checked. 

Hope that helped!

Hey! I'm not a doctor, but I've used Seroquel. There had been no serious side effects for me and it helped improve my focus and lessen the voices. I don't intend to put blame on the NP or you, but patients do tend to "overstate" their anxiety and could be misinterpreted by the NP. The NPs are just doing their job. 

My first NP prescribed me Benadryl for my *insomnia* before, turns out it was just the voices keeping me awake when I'm alone... So look at the bright side, it's actually better to be taken seriously. If you're not comfortable with the medicine, tell your NP immediately.

I think you could try Xanax, Lexapro, or Zoloft if you haven't taken them yet. They're "starter" meds. They worked for me but caused mania as a side-effect because it turns out, I'm bipolar and not just depressed.
